From 80df409e1a483676826a6c66e693dba6ac507751 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:21:05 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: ethernet: mtk_eth_soc: Fix use-after-free in metadata
 dst teardown

mtk_free_dev() calls metadata_dst_free() which frees the metadata_dst
with kfree() immediately, bypassing the RCU grace period.
In the RX path, skb_dst_set_noref() sets a non-refcounted pointer from
the skb to the metadata_dst. This function requires RCU read-side
protection and the dst must remain valid until all RCU readers complete.
Since metadata_dst_free() calls kfree() directly, a use-after-free can
occur if any skb still holds a noref pointer to the dst when the driver
tears it down.
Replace metadata_dst_free() with dst_release() which properly goes
through the refcount path: when the refcount drops to zero, it schedules
the actual free via call_rcu_hurry(), ensuring all RCU readers have
completed before the memory is freed.

Fixes: 2d7605a72906 ("net: ethernet: mtk_eth_soc: enable hardware DSA untagging")
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260602-airoha-mtk-metadata-uaf-fix-v1-2-3aaa99d83351@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mediatek/mtk_eth_soc.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mediatek/mtk_eth_soc.c
index 8d225bc9f063..7d771168b990 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mediatek/mtk_eth_soc.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mediatek/mtk_eth_soc.c
@@ -4491,7 +4491,7 @@ static int mtk_free_dev(struct mtk_eth *eth)
 	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(eth->dsa_meta); i++) {
 		if (!eth->dsa_meta[i])
 			break;
-		metadata_dst_free(eth->dsa_meta[i]);
+		dst_release(&eth->dsa_meta[i]->dst);
 	}
 
 	return 0;
-- 
2.34.1

### Modifications in each file

- **`drivers/net/ethernet/mediatek/mtk_eth_soc.c`**: In the function `mtk_free_dev`, the call `metadata_dst_free(eth->dsa_meta[i])` was replaced with `dst_release(&eth->dsa_meta[i]->dst)`.

### Relationships between modifications

The change is a single-line fix addressing a use-after-free vulnerability. The root cause was that `metadata_dst_free()` immediately frees the metadata dst via `kfree()`, bypassing the RCU grace period. Since the RX path uses `skb_dst_set_noref()` to set a non-refcounted pointer, the dst must remain valid until all RCU readers complete. By switching to `dst_release()`, the refcount-based deallocation path is used: when the refcount reaches zero, the actual free is scheduled via `call_rcu_hurry()`, ensuring all readers have finished before memory is reclaimed. This eliminates the use-after-free.

Here is the root cause:
Use-after-free vulnerability because `metadata_dst_free()` immediately frees the metadata dst via `kfree()`, bypassing the RCU grace period. In the RX path, `skb_dst_set_noref()` sets a non-refcounted pointer from the skb to the dst, requiring RCU read-side protection. Since the dst is freed without waiting for RCU readers, a use-after-free can occur when the driver tears down the metadata dst.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int mtk_free_dev(struct mtk_eth *eth)
 {
 	int i;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < MTK_MAX_DEVS; i++) {
 		if (!eth->netdev[i])
 			continue;
 		free_netdev(eth->netdev[i]);
 	}
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(eth->dsa_meta); i++) {
 		if (!eth->dsa_meta[i])
 			break;
-		metadata_dst_free(eth->dsa_meta[i]);
+		dst_release(&eth->dsa_meta[i]->dst);
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
